Articles

Concepts

Concepts

The vocabulary the other articles use, each term defined on a small fit, followed by the fitted object, its accessors and the rules the fitting functions enforce.

Models

Random slopes

Random slopes with a correlated or diagonal covariance: fit, check, extract per-group effects, predict and compare.

Spatial models

Areal and continuous spatial fields end to end: simulate, fit, check, map, predict and compare with a non-spatial fit.

Temporal models

Random-walk and autoregressive time trends end to end: simulate, fit, check, predict and compare with a fit without a time term.

Space-time models

Areal fields that change over time: additive space plus time, Knorr-Held interactions as Kronecker blocks, maps per time slice, forecasts, and which door fits which model.

Varying coefficients

Coefficients that change over space or time: spatially varying coefficients on a slope or the intercept, time-varying coefficients on a grid or at irregular times, checked against a constant coefficient, a parametric interaction and two priors.

Continuous fields with the SPDE

Matern fields on a triangular mesh in depth: the SPDE model, mesh construction and resolution, PC priors, mean and SD maps on a grid, and a comparison with non-spatial, NNGP and HSGP fits.

Spatial confounding and restricted spatial regression

What a spatial field does to the slope of a spatially smooth covariate, the two slopes a model can target, and how spatial_rsr() switches between them on areal and NNGP fields.

Joint models

Two response arms sharing one spatial field through a copy scale: simulate, fit, read the copy scale and its point mass at zero, compare with separate fits, predict where one arm has no data.

Latent factors

Many species counted at the same sites, sharing two latent site factors with a loading per species: simulate a long-format data set, fit it with tulpa(factors = ), and read loadings, the covariance between species they imply, and the site scores.

Categorical and ordinal responses

Responses that fall into one of several classes: the baseline-category logit for unordered classes and the cumulative logit for ordered ones, each simulated, fitted, checked, predicted and compared.

Workflows

Data formatting

The input tulpa() expects, built from a data frame, with random-effect terms, binomial trials, offsets and the validation errors.

Priors

The prior families, the defaults, priors on fixed effects and hyperparameters, and prior predictive checks.

Diagnostics

One Poisson areal model checked through every diagnostic tulpa offers: simulated residuals, spatial and temporal structure, sampler convergence, approximation reliability, model comparison and prior sensitivity, with a misspecified twin that shows what failing looks like.

Model comparison

Compare fits by marginal likelihood, Bayes factors, WAIC and LOO, and average models for prediction.

Troubleshooting

The errors and warnings a tulpa fit most often stops on, grouped by stage, each with the message as printed and a corrected call that runs.

Checkpointing

Save the progress of a long fit to disk, resume it after an interruption, and see the fingerprint refuse a file written for other inputs.

Custom latent blocks

Write a latent block in R or C++ and fit it at every inference tier.

EM + Laplace

Fit a model with a discrete latent variable by writing two callbacks for the EM + Laplace driver, then correct its standard errors by multiple imputation or Gibbs sampling.

Case studies

Case study: sudden infant deaths in North Carolina

An applied areal analysis on real county data: expected counts as an offset, non-spatial, ICAR and BYM2 fits, risk maps with exceedance probabilities, residual Moran’s I, a prior check and the limits of an ecological question.

Background

Inference modes

The three inference tiers, how mode = “auto” chooses between them, and what each backend costs and guarantees.

Identifiability

The maths of each alias and weakly identified hyperparameter behind tulpa’s fields and random effects, with stress tests that show how many regions, locations or groups recovery needs.

Reliability diagnostics

Read the Pareto k-hat that scores whether a deterministic approximation can be trusted, and what to do when it is high.

Simulation-based calibration

Check that an inference algorithm is calibrated across the generative model with simulation-based calibration.

Compatibility with lme4, glmmTMB, brms and INLA

The same models fitted in tulpa and in lme4, glmmTMB, brms and INLA with matched settings and priors: measured agreement, a syntax map, the documented differences, timings, and when the other package fits the task better.
